question: Two card branches hold finished, gated work that reached neither their run branch nor dev and have sat invisible for a month. What happens to them?
proposal: Leave both branches in place and record them as a backlog entry (B-442) rather than deleting them or merging them to recover the work.

votes.note: Neither branch blocks a milestone card; recording preserves the option to re-apply when a slate has room, at no cost tonight.
They will keep surfacing in every worktree sweep until picked up, which is noise in a check whose value depends on an empty result meaning something.

Merging is unsafe: patch-equivalence is not merge-safety — the base files moved since these patches applied, so a three-way merge can re-insert a block at a new location (B-133). Re-application off dev is the only safe recovery.

cited.statement: A decision number, backlog handle, ledger section, card ID, key-result name, gate label or commit SHA carries no meaning on its own. Attach what it identifies, in a few words, on first use in any document or message — "decision 126 (reads move to RxDB, writes stay on REST)", not "decision 126". Keep the identifier; never let it travel alone. This binds the written record too: the ledger, handoffs and commit bodies are where bare numbers accumulate and are hardest to decode later, because nobody reads a ledger linearly. A short gloss beats a perfect one.
cited.fit: Recording the branches with what they contain (B-35 RLS fixture guard; demo:sync exit-code guard) rather than a bare branch name is what makes the entry actionable a month later.

cited.statement: Red-first evidence is a named gate row in the ladder — a card that has not shown its red cannot merge. An obligation that matters gets a gate, not a reminder in a launch prompt.
cited.fit: Both branches carry their own red-first evidence and green gates, so the work is gate-complete and worth preserving rather than discarding.

weighing: PM reads this as low-severity because nothing is blocked; PjM and engineering both read medium, for different reasons — sweep noise and merge hazard. The merge hazard (B-133) is what rules out the recovery option that would otherwise clear the noise, so the two medium votes point the same way: keep the work, do not merge it. Delete was rejected because the guards would have to be rebuilt from scratch when the bugs they caught recur.

question: The card reported done_when clause 2 (attempt-record distinguishability) as MET, disclosing only that the proof was stitched from two runs. Triage found the discriminating value is unreachable in shipped code. Accept the clause as landed, or rule it un-landed?
proposal: Rule clause 2 NOT landed, file B-438, and bar policy_unresolved from being cited as evidence until the policy source attaches outside startSync.

votes.note: The clause is the audit trail for why an offline override was allowed on a high-value code; a column that is a constant cannot answer that question for the operator later.
Third consecutive run where a clean G6 rested on a scope claim an independent reproduction falsified; accepting it would let the pattern continue unnamed.

Verified in-browser: attach() runs only inside startSync, gated on a localStorage key nothing writes, so unresolved() is false against an empty Map. The e2e asserting the value stubs both functions with literals.

cited.statement: Red-first evidence is a named gate row in the ladder — a card that has not shown its red cannot merge. An obligation that matters gets a gate, not a reminder in a launch prompt.
cited.fit: A red-first gate proves the test catches the defect; here the assertion passes against stubs, so it never sampled the shipped path at all.

cited.statement: before closing anything under P-3, state the condition you sampled — load, concurrency, data volume, journal depth — and whether it is the condition the original report described. *"Could not reproduce on a quiet box"* is a finding; *"could not reproduce"* is not. Absence of reproduction in N legs bounds a rate conditional on the sampled condition only.
cited.weight: strong — this is the corollary that makes P-3 safe to apply; applying P-3 without it is how a live bug gets closed.
cited.fit: Directly on point — a reproduction must sample the RIGHT condition or it proves nothing; stubbing both the policy fn and the unresolved fn samples the stub, not the replica.

weighing: PM votes top because the column is an accountability record, not an internal detail. Engineering and PjM both medium, and neither disputes the mechanism — it was verified by browser probe rather than argued. No cited preference opposes: P-4 in particular is squarely for, since the whole question is whether an assertion against literals constitutes evidence about a shipped path. B-432 itself is unaffected and stays closed, so ruling clause 2 un-landed costs nothing already earned.
reasons: top-severity questions are the operator's — no number of citations clears them
